etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Modern Dutch slee, from Middle Dutch slede, ultimately from Proto-Germanic *slidô. Doublet of sled and further related to slide.

definitions.definition: A vehicle, generally pulled by an animal, which moves over snow or ice on runners, used for transporting persons or goods. (contrast "sled", which is smaller)

quote.citation: 2023 December 27, David Turner, “Silent lines...”, in RAIL, number 999, page 29:
quote.text: In 1958, it was reported that for "the fourth year in succession, staff of four South London stations have combined to decorate the booking hall at Peckham Rye station". They installed a nativity scene, models of Father Christmas, and a sleigh driven by huskies, and Christmas trees were placed around the station.

definitions.definition: To ride or drive a sleigh.

etymologies.etymologyHTML: sleigh (comparative sleigher, superlative sleighest)
